Alice Chen.hiring_brief:
Alice Chen is a textbook fit for this role. Eight years of Python in high-throughput fintech — not adjacent experience, not transferable skills, but the exact work: Stripe and Plaid integrations, PCI-DSS compliance ownership, async microservices at scale processing billions in transactions. She has done this job. Her current stack (FastAPI, asyncio, PostgreSQL, Kubernetes, Kafka) maps to every line of the job description without translation required. The open-source Python maintainership is a meaningful differentiator — it's a signal of technical depth and community engagement that almost no other candidate can show.

The only honest concern is compensation positioning. An 8-year fintech engineer with her profile is likely expecting somewhere in the $125–145k range. The posted range ($160–195k) actually works in your favor here — but if you're trying to close her below $150k, expect friction. Clarify the budget ceiling before you go deep in the process, not after.

Move her forward immediately. She is the candidate you benchmark everyone else against.
strengths: Direct Stripe/Plaid/ACH integration ownership in production — not exposure, she built and maintained these integrations at scale
PCI-DSS compliance leadership at her current company — rare hands-on compliance experience that is explicitly required for this role
Open-source Python maintainership — signals technical depth and community reputation that reflects well on the team
Mentorship track record with junior engineers — the JD explicitly calls this out as required
8 years pure fintech experience — zero domain translation required, she understands payments constraints from day one
concerns: AWS-primary background may mean a GCP learning curve if the team leans that direction — the JD accepts either, but worth flagging early
Alice Chen.salary_signal: $125–145k estimated based on 8 years at high-growth fintech with senior ownership scope. The posted range ($160–195k) is above this estimate — she will likely negotiate toward $170–180k at midpoint.

Grace Kim.hiring_brief:
Grace Kim is nearly indistinguishable from the top of this pool on paper, and that is a strong statement. Seven years of fintech, 8M events/day throughput, PCI-DSS Level 1 ownership, and every required technical skill checked without gaps. Her background at a payments-focused company means she has already solved the hard distributed systems problems this role will ask her to solve again — she brings proven headroom, not just theoretical knowledge.

One thing worth probing in the first conversation: her throughput experience actually exceeds the JD's stated scale. There is a real risk she underestimates the role's complexity going in, or worse, finds it unchallenging once she's in. Ask her directly what she's hoping to learn or build in this role — the answer will tell you whether she's energized by the work or just making a safe career move.

Advance her alongside Alice Chen. If you can only make one offer, Alice's open-source track record and mentorship depth are the tiebreaker. But Grace is a legitimate first choice and would excel here.

Frank Nguyen.hiring_brief:
Frank Nguyen has the deepest individual technical profile in this pool. Nine-plus years, Staff Engineer title, gRPC implementation experience (almost no other candidate has this), Kafka ownership, and PCI-DSS recertification leadership. On paper, he is overqualified for a Senior Engineer role — and that is both an asset and a risk that must be resolved before you go deep in the process.

The critical question is motivation. A Staff Engineer applying for a Senior role is making a deliberate title step-down. That can mean several things: he is leaving a dysfunctional environment and wants solid, stable work; he is prioritizing compensation range over title; or his current company is struggling and he needs to move. Each of those is acceptable — but you need to know which it is. A candidate who is running toward something builds differently than one who is running away from something.

If his motivation is genuine and his expectations about autonomy match what a Senior IC role offers here, he is your strongest technical hire. Run the motivation conversation first. If it holds up, advance him immediately.
strengths: 9+ years at Staff Engineer depth — will independently own architecture decisions without management overhead
gRPC expertise — rare skill explicitly listed as nice-to-have; virtually no other candidate in this pool has it
